summary: France does not collect ethnic statistics. Police data give child victims of sexual violence, family violence and homicide by French or foreign nationality, and suspects by nationality for all victims together; a government survey gives childhood violence by migration background. There are no national neglect data by origin and nothing for online exploitation.

nations.National (SSMSI, SSER, INSEE): Police victim and suspect open data by French/foreign nationality since 2016; trafficking report with nationality groups; surveys with migration background.
nations.Overseas departments: Included in the SSMSI France totals.

groups.label: Neither immigrant nor child of immigrants

european_title: Not recorded by any French source
european_note: French law and practice exclude ethnic statistics from official data. Sources record nationality (French or foreign, sometimes by continent) or, in surveys, migration background. 'French' includes naturalised citizens of any origin and 'foreign' mixes Europeans and non-Europeans, so ethnic Europeans cannot be identified for victims or perpetrators.
proxy_note: France records nationality (French or foreign) or migration background, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual violence against children (police)
harms.intro: Police and gendarmerie recorded 76,167 child victims of sexual violence in 2025, including 25,786 victims of rape or attempted rape. Suspects are published by nationality only for all victims together: 84,937 people were suspected of sexual violence against victims of any age.

victims.scope: France, police-recorded child victims (under 18) of sexual violence, 2025
victims.share_note: Nationality, not ethnicity: French statistics never record ethnic origin. 'French' includes naturalised citizens; how dual nationals are coded is not documented in the dataset. The dataset publishes no 'unknown nationality' category (French + foreign = total).
victims.rate_label: child victims per 100,000 children of the same nationality group
victims.rate_note: Calculated here: SSMSI counts divided by INSEE 2022 census population by nationality (table NAT1). INSEE publishes under-15 and 15-24 bands, so under-18s are estimated as under-15 plus 3/10 of 15-24. Approximate; census year 2022, crime year 2025.

perpetrators.scope: France, suspects of sexual violence against victims of all ages, 2025
perpetrators.rate_label: suspects per 100,000 residents of the same nationality group (all ages)
perpetrators.rate_note: Calculated here with INSEE 2022 census population by nationality (all ages). Crude rates, not adjusted for age or sex: foreign residents are on average younger and more often male.
perpetrators.share_note: Nationality, not ethnicity: French statistics never record ethnic origin. 'French' includes naturalised citizens; how dual nationals are coded is not documented in the dataset. The dataset publishes no 'unknown nationality' category (French + foreign = total). Suspects (mis en cause) in solved cases, not convicted offenders. Includes 21,160 suspects who were themselves minors. Not child-victim-specific.

cross.text: Suspect tables are not split by the victim's age or nationality, so suspects of offences against children cannot be separated and no victim-by-suspect table exists.

harms.label: Trafficking and exploitation
harms.intro: Police and gendarmerie recorded 2,127 victims of trafficking or exploitation in 2024, 22.9% of them minors, and 2,106 suspects. Minors were 35.4% of victims of pimping (proxénétisme). Nationality is published for all ages only.

victims.share_note: Nationality groups as rounded in the report text (Infostat Justice 203, figure 4). Not split by age: about 490 of these victims were minors. Among victims of pimping, 65% were French and 20% from the Americas.

perpetrators.scope: France, suspects of trafficking or exploitation, 2024
perpetrators.share_note: As rounded in the report text. 74.6% of suspects of pimping were French. Not split by the age of the victim.

harms.label: Online child sexual exploitation
harms.intro: None of the 18 indicators in the SSMSI victim and suspect datasets covers child sexual abuse material or online exploitation, and no nationality breakdown for these offences was found.

perpetrators.text: Not published by nationality or any origin variable.

breakdown.why: SSMSI open data: 76,167 child victims of sexual violence in 2025 by French/foreign nationality; suspects by nationality for all victim ages only. Binary nationality proxy; ethnic statistics are not collected.

63,059 child victims of intra-family physical violence by French/foreign nationality (2025); the official Genese survey gives parental violence by migration background. Suspects only for all victims of intra-family violence.
No national neglect statistics by any origin variable; the ONPE notes there is no homogeneous national count of reasons for protection.
95 child homicide victims in 2025 by French/foreign nationality (child-specific, unlike Germany); suspects by nationality for all ages.
Trafficking victims (2,127, 23% minors) and suspects (2,106) by nationality group, 2024, all ages only.
No nationality or origin published for online child sexual exploitation victims or suspects.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: France scores 24% on the stricter scale (20-40%). France does not collect ethnic statistics. The police publish child victims of sexual violence, intra-family violence and homicide by French or foreign nationality, and suspects by nationality for all ages, all as a capped proxy. There are no national neglect data by origin and nothing for online exploitation. The 25% cap for countries without ethnicity data would apply, but France is already below it.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)

ssmsi_v.limitations: French vs foreign only; no ethnicity (not collected in France); small cells suppressed; no unknown-nationality category.

ssmsi_m.limitations: French vs foreign only; not split by victim age, so suspects of offences against children cannot be isolated.
